label: 24V 24W gigabit passive PoE injector
description: Single-port passive 24V PoE adapter that feeds 24 VDC at 1 A (24 W) over the spare pairs to an airMAX radio or other 24V-only device. It does no 802.3af/at detection or classification, so it will apply 24V to any device plugged in regardless of what that device expects.

label: 48V 24W gigabit passive PoE injector
description: Passive 48 VDC / 0.5 A (24 W) gigabit injector for Ubiquiti gear that expects always-on 48V on the spare pairs (older airMAX, UniFi APs, airFiber links). It is not 802.3af/at: there is no handshake, so a standards-compliant PD that waits for detection will never power up from it.

label: 802.3af 15.4W gigabit PoE injector
description: IEEE 802.3af-compliant single-port injector that auto-detects the powered device and delivers up to 15.4 W at 48V over gigabit Ethernet. Because it performs real af detection/classification it powers standard PoE cameras and APs safely, but it cannot feed 802.3at 25.5W loads.

label: Gigabit passive PoE injector (18-57V pass-through)
description: Bare passive injector with no PSU: it takes 18-57 VDC on a DC jack and pushes that same voltage out on pins 4,5 (+) and 7,8 (-). Output power is whatever the attached adapter supplies (the 24 W / 24V 1A figure shown is the common pairing), and since it never negotiates, 802.3af/at PDs must not be connected to it.

label: 4-port 802.3at gigabit PoE midspan (30W/port)
description: Rack/desk midspan that splices 802.3at power into four existing gigabit links, giving 30 W per port (120 W total) to APs, PTZ cameras and phones without replacing the switch. It sits between the switch and the devices and negotiates af/at per port, so passive-PoE gear will not come up on it.

label: 8-port managed 802.3at PoE midspan (30W/port, 240W)
description: 1U managed midspan that adds 802.3af/at power to eight gigabit data links, 30 W per port and 240 W total with battery-backed charging. Per-port power is schedulable and metered over the network, which makes it the usual choice for camera runs where the switch has no PoE.

label: 802.3af to 12V DC gigabit PoE splitter
description: Inline splitter that accepts 802.3af PoE on one RJ45 and hands out clean 12 VDC at 1 A (12 W) on a 2.1x5.5 mm barrel while passing gigabit data through to the device. It lets a 12V-only camera or media player run from a PoE switch; it draws standard af power, so it works on any compliant PSE but not on a passive injector.

label: Gigabit 802.3af/at PoE extender (100m per hop)
description: Two-port inline extender with a PoE IN and a PoE OUT jack that regenerates both gigabit data and 802.3af/at power for another 100 m, chainable up to 500 m. It passes the PSE's negotiated power through with a small loss rather than creating a new budget, so downstream watts come out of the upstream switch port.

label: 60W 802.3bt Type 3 multi-gig PoE injector
description: Single-port 802.3bt Type 3 injector that negotiates up to 60 W at 56 V across all four pairs and carries 2.5G data, sized for Wi-Fi 6/6E APs and heaters/PTZ domes. Because it is a true bt PSE with LLDP and class-based power, it will only hand out 60 W to a device that asks for it.

label: 60W 802.3bt outdoor single-port midspan
description: Weatherproof single-port midspan that injects 60 W of 802.3bt (Type 3) power into a gigabit link, made for pole- or wall-mounted cameras and radios. It performs full bt detection, so it powers standards-based 60W PDs and refuses passive 24V/48V devices.

label: 90W 802.3bt Type 4 managed PoE midspan
description: SNMP-managed single-port midspan delivering the full 90 W of 802.3bt Type 4 at 56 V/1.6 A over four pairs into a gigabit link, for high-power APs, laptops over PoE and 4K PTZ cameras. It negotiates class 8 power and reports per-port consumption, so the 90 W is only committed after the PD is classified.

label: 802.3at 30W gigabit single-port midspan
description: Single-port 802.3at midspan that inserts 30 W of PoE+ into one existing gigabit cable run, the standard fix for a lone AP or camera on a non-PoE switch. It classifies the PD per 802.3af/at and backs off to 15.4 W for af devices, so 802.3bt loads are not supported.
